Service 1 of 6

Automation Repair

Most automations don't crash loudly. They fail on one missing field and keep going.

A renamed column, an expired token, a vendor API change. The automation still looks like it's running while the data downstream goes wrong. viabolat finds the exact cause and fixes it, instead of patching around it.

What viabolat does

  • Root-cause diagnosis of every failing step
  • Fix or rebuild, with error handling and alerts so the next failure is loud
  • Documentation and handoff, so you know what changed

Pricing

  • Fix and Walk Away: $1,500 to $2,500, fixed
  • Fix and Maintain: $1,800 to $2,800, plus $300 to $500 a month
  • Urgent fixes in 48 to 72 hours, rebuilds in 7 to 10 days

Service 2 of 6

Data Validation

If your team re-checks every report by hand, nobody trusts the data.

Duplicate rows, blank fields, dates in three formats, totals that don't match the source. Bad data spreads into every report built on it. viabolat adds checks where the data comes in, so problems get flagged instead of averaged in.

What viabolat does

  • Data-quality audit: where records break, duplicate or go missing
  • Automated validation rules and de-duplication
  • Alerts, or a review sheet for records that fail a check

Data Pipelines

If the same export, clean and paste happens every week, it can run on a schedule.

Pulling data out of one tool, cleaning it in a spreadsheet and pasting it into another eats hours nobody tracks, and every manual step is a chance for a typo. viabolat builds scheduled pipelines in Python or the automation tool you already use, with a log of every run.

Service 4 of 6

System Integrations

Every time someone retypes data from one system into another, you pay for it twice.

When two systems don't share data, a person becomes the bridge: retyping orders, syncing contacts, reconciling invoices. It's slow, it's error-prone, and it stops when that person is out. viabolat connects the systems directly, with error handling for the day one of them changes.

What viabolat does

  • Integration plan: what syncs, in which direction, how often
  • API and webhook build with retries, token refresh and error alerts
  • Documentation of every connection
